title_en: Supreme People's Court Rules on Security Checks by Judicial Police of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Rules on Security Checks by Judicial Police

Issued by the Supreme People's Court, Document No. Fa Fa [2004] 14

Article 1. These Rules are formulated in accordance with the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Public Security of the People's Republic of China, the Rules of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, and other laws and regulations, in order to ensure the normal conduct of trial activities in the People's Courts and to standardize the security check work of the Judicial Police of the People's Courts.

Article 2. "Security check" refers to the official act by which the Judicial Police of the People's Courts, in accordance with the needs of trial work and pursuant to law, prevent restricted articles, controlled articles, flammable and explosive articles, highly corrosive articles, and other dangerous articles from entering the court premises, thereby ensuring the personal safety of persons participating in court proceedings and the smooth progress of trial work.

Article 3. The security check work for trial courts of the People's Courts shall adhere to the principles of strictness, thoroughness, and civility. It shall be organized and implemented by the Judicial Police departments of the People's Courts at all levels, with assistance from relevant departments.

When performing security checks, Judicial Police must dress according to regulations, maintain a high degree of vigilance, and present a neat and orderly appearance. Generally, there shall be no fewer than two persons; when the workload of security checks is heavy, the number of personnel shall be appropriately increased.

Article 4. Trial courts at all levels shall be equipped with security check gates, hand-held metal detectors, item lockers, and other necessary security check equipment. Courts with the relevant conditions may equip themselves with X-ray detection equipment.

The security check gate shall generally be placed on one side of the main entrance that must be passed through to enter the trial court of the court, establishing a dedicated security check passage. A notice board stating matters related to the security check shall be placed in front of the passage. The hand-held detector shall be used as a supplementary detection means for manual inspection when the person being inspected sets off the alarm of the security check gate. The item locker shall be placed on one side of the security check gate for the temporary storage of items.

The security check equipment shall be kept in the custody of designated personnel from the Judicial Police department. Before use, the equipment shall be turned on and tested to ensure it is in good working condition. For hand-held detectors, ensure the batteries are adequately charged and the device is in good condition.

Article 5. During the security check, two basic work positions shall be established: the guide and the inspector.

The main duty of the guide is to examine or register the identification documents of the person being inspected and guide them into the security check gate. The main duty of the inspector is to conduct personal security checks at the security check gate and security checks of items carried on the person.

Article 6. When Judicial Police perform security checks:
(1) For public prosecutors, lawyers, and other personnel appearing in court to perform their duties according to law, valid identification documents shall be examined and registered.
(2) For litigation participants, third parties, and persons attending the trial as observers, in addition to examining and registering their identification documents, personal security checks and security checks of items carried on the person shall also be conducted.

Article 7. The following persons shall not be permitted to enter the court premises:
(1) Persons without identification documents, or those using forged or fraudulently obtained identification documents of others.
(2) Minors (except those approved by the court).
(3) Persons who are mentally ill or intoxicated.
(4) Persons who have been deprived of political rights, are serving a sentence outside prison, or are under residential surveillance or released on bail pending trial.
(5) Persons who refuse to undergo security checks or do not follow the arrangements of the security check personnel.
(6) Other persons who may potentially disrupt the order of the court trial.

Article 8. The following items shall not be carried into the court premises:
(1) Restricted items such as various recording, video, and photographic equipment not permitted by the court.
(2) Controlled items such as firearms, knives, and other instruments or sticks with similar functions that are prohibited for private possession.
(3) Dangerous articles such as flammable and explosive articles, and highly corrosive articles.
(4) Other items that may potentially disrupt the order of the court trial.

Article 9. Examination and registration of identification documents:
(1) Check whether the document has exceeded its validity period.
(2) Check whether the photograph, name, age, sex, and other relevant elements match the holder of the document.
(3) Check whether the document for permission to observe the trial matches the case and the court being observed.
(4) A dedicated registration book shall be established to register the documents of the persons being inspected.

Article 10. Personal security checks:
(1) The guide prompts the person being inspected to remove items carried on their person and place them on the worktable placed near the security check gate.
(2) For persons being inspected who set off the alarm of the security check gate, the inspector shall order them to pass through the gate again for another check or conduct a re-inspection using manual security check methods. When manual checks are used, personal security checks of female persons being inspected shall be conducted by female Judicial Police.
(3) Manual inspection includes two methods: hand-held detector inspection and hand search. The specific sequence for conducting manual inspection is: from top to bottom, from outside to inside, from front to back. That is, starting from the collar of the person being inspected, proceed to the outer sides of both shoulders, the palms of both hands, the inner sides of both shoulders, the armpits, the back, the lower back, the crotch area, both legs, and the feet. When conducting hand-held detector inspection, the movement of the hand-held metal detector shall be steady and at a uniform speed. When conducting hand searches, the emphasis shall be on "touching and pressing," with appropriate and even force.
(4) Persons being inspected whose check raises suspicion shall be questioned.
(5) After the inspection is completed, the person being inspected shall be prompted to retrieve their belongings.

Article 11. Security checks of items carried on the person:
(1) Courts equipped with X-ray detection equipment shall conduct security detection checks on all bags and cases. For bags and cases that raise suspicion, a manual check shall also be conducted with the bag or case opened in the presence of the person.
(2) When conducting bag-opening checks, attention shall be paid to the bottom, corners, and outer pockets of the bag or case, and hidden compartments shall be watched for.
(3) When inspecting items such as bags (pouches), handle them with care to avoid damage or soiling. Items involving personal privacy shall be handled with appropriate care in placement.
(4) Items that raise suspicion shall be questioned about. For controlled items and dangerous articles, control shall be established first, followed by questioning.
(5) After the inspection is completed, assist in tidying up the bags and cases, and prompt the person being inspected to retrieve their belongings.

Article 12. Handling of restricted items, controlled items, and dangerous articles that are discovered:
(1) Restricted items shall be subject to a storage system. The owner's identification document and the number and model of restricted items shall be registered. After confirmation and signature by the owner, a storage token shall be issued. Restricted items shall be temporarily stored in the item locker. After the conclusion of the court hearing, the owner may retrieve the stored items upon presenting their identification document and the token, after confirming that all items are complete and undamaged and signing for them. Stored items shall be properly kept to prevent damage or loss.
(2) Controlled items such as firearms and knives not permitted for private possession shall be confiscated and handled uniformly by the Judicial Police department.
(3) Dangerous articles such as flammable and explosive articles, and highly corrosive articles, and other items not allowed into the court that are discovered, shall, after ensuring there is no danger, be handled by means of the storage system for restricted items or be confiscated in accordance with relevant regulations.

Article 13. Persons being inspected who refuse to undergo security checks or do not follow the arrangements of the security check personnel shall be prevented from entering the trial court. If they do not heed the advice, compulsory measures may be taken according to law.

Article 14. If Judicial Police performing security check duties abandon their posts, are negligent, commit dereliction of duty, or engage in other such conduct, causing serious consequences, they shall be dealt with in light of the circumstances, in accordance with the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, the Measures for Investigation of Liability for Illegal Adjudication by Judicial Personnel of the People's Courts (Trial Implementation), the Measures for Imposition of Disciplinary Sanctions in the People's Courts (Trial Implementation), and other relevant provisions. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.

Article 15. These Rules shall take effect from the date of promulgation.

May 24, 2004
